simple.meaning: מַעַר (maʻar) is a Hebrew word meaning “a nude place , i.e. (literally) the pudenda , or (figuratively) a vacant space.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַעַר (H4626) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 7:36, with occurrences in 1 Kings, Nahum.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעַר (H4626) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַעַר (H4626) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַעַר (maʻar) / H4626 is traced through 1 Kings 7:36, Nahum 3:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4626. maar [ מַעֲרֶה ], מַ֫עַר noun [masculine] bare, naked place (hence Μαραθών , Marathon, according to Lewy Fremdw. 144 ); — 1 bare place , or space: construct מִמַּעֲרִהגָּֿ֑בַע Judg 20:33 bare (open) space of Geba' (si vera 1.; but see II. מַעֲרָב ); כְּמַעַראִֿישׁ 1Kin 7:36 according to the clear space on each (plate, see לוּחַ ). 2 suffix מַעְרֵח Nahum 3:5 figurative of Nineveh ( pudenda exposed in shameful punishment; compare עֶרְוָה ).
